articles.title: AWS IAM fundamentals: root user, users, groups, roles and policies
articles.scope: Explains that IAM is an authorization system scoped to each account, not a directory. Covers the root user and the tasks only root can do, IAM users vs groups vs roles, long-term vs temporary credentials, access keys, MFA and password policies, and ARNs. Contrasts it with Entra ID (tenant directory) plus Azure RBAC, so the reader can say why AWS pushes humans to federation and workloads to roles.

articles.title: IAM policy types compared: identity-based, resource-based, permissions boundaries, session policies, SCPs, RCPs and ACLs
articles.scope: Sets out each policy type by where it attaches, whether it can grant or only limit, and which principals it affects. Covers AWS managed vs customer managed vs inline policies and which services support resource-based policies. Ends with a decision table for which lever to use in a given situation.

articles.title: How AWS evaluates a request: policy evaluation logic within and across accounts
articles.scope: Walks the full evaluation flow: explicit deny, then RCPs, SCPs, resource-based policies, identity-based policies, permissions boundaries and session policies. Shows how the outcome differs for role-ARN vs role-session principals, and why cross-account access must be allowed on both sides. Covers special cases such as KMS key policies, so the reader can predict any allow/deny result and explain an AccessDenied message.

articles.title: IAM policy language reference: elements, operators, policy variables and global condition keys
articles.scope: Reference for Effect, Action/NotAction, Resource/NotResource, Principal/NotPrincipal and Condition, the condition operators, IfExists, ForAllValues/ForAnyValue and policy variables. Includes a curated table of global condition keys such as aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:ResourceOrgID, aws:SourceVpce, aws:VpceOrgID, aws:RequestedRegion, aws:PrincipalTag, aws:SecureTransport, aws:SourceArn and aws:CalledVia. Snippets are given in JSON, CDK (C#/Python) and Terraform.

articles.title: AWS STS and role assumption: trust policies, cross-account access, role chaining and federation APIs
articles.scope: Contrasts trust policies with permissions policies. Covers AssumeRole, AssumeRoleWithSAML, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, GetSessionToken and GetFederationToken; session duration and the one-hour role-chaining limit; external ID against the confused deputy; source identity, session tags and regional endpoints. Compares cross-account access via role assumption, resource-based policies and AWS RAM, with C# and Python SDK samples.

articles.title: Workload credentials on AWS: instance profiles, execution roles, IAM Roles Anywhere, OIDC federation and outbound identity federation
articles.scope: Compares the ways workloads get temporary credentials: EC2 instance profiles, Lambda and ECS task roles, EKS (linked to the containers section), IAM Roles Anywhere for on-premises machines, OIDC federation for CI such as GitHub Actions with mandatory claim checks, and STS GetWebIdentityToken for AWS-to-external calls. Shows cross-cloud federation in both directions (Entra workload identity to AWS, AWS JWT to Azure). Builds on security/workload-identity without duplicating it.

articles.title: Human access to AWS: IAM users vs IAM SAML/OIDC federation vs IAM Identity Center vs AWS Directory Service
articles.scope: Decision guide for workforce access. Compares IAM users, direct IAM identity-provider federation, IAM Identity Center with an external IdP such as Entra ID, and the directory options: AWS Managed Microsoft AD, AD Connector and Simple AD. Explains when to federate a directory with IAM roles and how each option fits multi-account estates and Windows workloads.

articles.title: IAM Identity Center: permission sets, account assignments, identity sources and multi-Region
articles.scope: Explains organization vs account instances, the three identity source types (Identity Center directory, Active Directory, external IdP with SAML 2.0 and SCIM), permission sets and account assignments, and the access portal and CLI sign-in. Also covers ABAC attributes, delegated administration, trusted identity propagation, customer managed KMS keys and multi-Region replication (2026). Maps each construct to Entra ID groups, Azure RBAC role assignments and PIM, with fidelity ratings.

articles.title: ABAC on AWS: principal tags, resource tags, session tags and scaling permissions
articles.scope: Shows how to scale authorization with aws:PrincipalTag, aws:ResourceTag, aws:RequestTag and aws:TagKeys conditions. Covers session tags passed from an IdP, transitive tags, Identity Center attributes for access control, tag governance with tag policies, and services that do not support tag-based conditions. Weighs ABAC against RBAC and links to security/iam for the neutral concept.

articles.title: Permissions boundaries: safely delegating IAM administration without privilege escalation
articles.scope: Explains the intersection semantics of boundaries and the iam:PermissionsBoundary condition that forces delegated admins to attach one. Covers blocking escalation paths (iam:PassRole, policy versioning) and how boundaries differ from SCPs and session policies. Contrasts with Azure's constrained role-assignment delegation (ABAC conditions) as a partial equivalent.

articles.title: Least privilege and access troubleshooting: IAM Access Analyzer, policy simulator, last-accessed data and AccessDenied messages
articles.scope: Uses external, internal and unused access analyzers, policy validation, custom policy checks in CI, and policy generation from CloudTrail activity. Covers the credential report and the policy simulator, plus decoding AccessDenied messages that name the blocking policy type. The reader leaves with a repeatable least-privilege review and triage process.

articles.title: Amazon Cognito: user pools vs identity pools for customer and app identity
articles.scope: Contrasts user pools (an OIDC user directory with managed login, MFA and federation) with identity pools (which exchange tokens for temporary AWS credentials). Covers feature plans, token types, and integration with ALB, API Gateway and Amazon Verified Permissions. Rates the mapping to Entra External ID and shows token validation in ASP.NET Core and Python.

articles.title: AWS multi-account strategy: accounts as isolation boundaries and recommended OU structures
articles.scope: Explains why the account is AWS's hard boundary for blast radius, quotas and billing, and walks through the recommended OUs (Security, Infrastructure, Workloads, Sandbox, Policy Staging, Suspended, Exceptions). Covers account vending and when to split accounts. Maps the AWS model to Azure tenants, management groups, subscriptions and resource groups, with an honest note on where subscription-as-boundary differs.

articles.title: AWS Organizations and AWS RAM: management account, OUs, consolidated billing, trusted access, delegated administrators and resource sharing
articles.scope: Covers the organization root, the management and member accounts, all-features vs consolidated-billing-only mode, consolidated billing and RI/Savings Plans sharing, trusted access, delegated administrators, and account migration and closure. Explains AWS RAM sharing of subnets, Transit Gateways, Resolver rules, prefix lists and Capacity Reservations, including the organization-only option. Includes CDK and Terraform for building an OU tree.

articles.title: Organization policies compared: SCPs vs RCPs vs declarative policies (EC2, tag, backup, AI opt-out and more)
articles.scope: Contrasts principal ceilings (SCPs), resource ceilings (RCPs) and control-plane configuration enforcement (declarative policies). Covers inheritance, effective policies, impact on the management account and on service-linked roles, size and attachment limits, and the full list of declarative types as of 2026, including Amazon EC2 policies, VPC Block Public Access and VPC Encryption Controls. Compares each with Azure Policy effects and deny assignments.

articles.title: Organization guardrails and security baseline: SCP patterns, centralized root access, delegated admins and break-glass
articles.scope: Catalogs proven guardrails: deny leaving the organization, Region deny with exemptions, protecting baseline roles and trails, and denying root usage. Covers centralized root access management for member accounts, MFA and break-glass design, delegated admin placement for security services, an organization trail, and a Config aggregator. Also covers safe guardrail rollout with a Policy Staging OU.

articles.title: Data perimeters on AWS: identity, resource and network perimeters with SCPs, RCPs and VPC endpoint policies
articles.scope: Builds the three perimeters: trusted identities, trusted resources and expected networks. Uses aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:ResourceOrgID, aws:SourceVpce, the 2025 aws:VpceOrgID family, RCPs and endpoint policies, with service-principal exceptions handled correctly. Links to security/cloud-security for the neutral zero-trust framing and rates the mapping to Azure Private Link, network security perimeter and Azure Policy.

articles.title: AWS Control Tower and landing zones: controls, Account Factory, AFT, drift and landing zone 4.0
articles.scope: Explains the landing zone, the control behaviors (preventive, detective, proactive) and guidance levels (mandatory, strongly recommended, elective), the Control Catalog, drift and its remediation, and Account Factory vs AFT vs CfCT. Covers landing zone 4.0's optional integrations and flexible OU structure, and Landing Zone Accelerator as an alternative. Compares with Azure Landing Zones (partial).

articles.title: AWS Config: recording, rules, conformance packs, aggregators and automatic remediation
articles.scope: Covers the configuration recorder and recording modes, configuration items and history, service-linked recorders, managed vs custom (Lambda and Guard) rules, proactive evaluation, and conformance packs including the 2026 AI/ML packs. Also covers organization aggregators, advanced queries and remediation through Systems Manager Automation. Compares with Azure Policy compliance and Resource Graph change analysis.

articles.title: AWS CloudTrail for governance: event types, organization trails, log integrity and centralized audit
articles.scope: Covers management, data, network activity and Insights events; trails vs event data stores; organization and multi-Region trails; and log file integrity validation and SSE-KMS. Explains centralized delivery to a Log Archive account, event enrichment, and the fact that CloudTrail Lake closed to new customers on 2026-05-31. Compares with the Azure Activity Log and resource logs.

articles.title: Governance and audit services compared: Organizations policies vs Control Tower vs Config vs CloudTrail vs CloudWatch vs Trusted Advisor
articles.scope: Sorts each service into prevent, detect, record, observe or advise, answering 'what changed', 'who did it', 'is it compliant' and 'how is it behaving'. Adds Audit Manager and Artifact as pointers into the security-services section. Settles the classic CLF and associate-exam confusion with one matrix and an Azure column.

articles.title: AWS tagging strategy: tag policies, cost allocation tags, ABAC tags and enforcement
articles.scope: Designs a tag taxonomy (cost center, owner, environment, data classification) and enforces it with tag policies, SCP tag conditions, Config rules and IaC defaults. Covers activating user-defined and AWS-generated cost allocation tags, Tag Editor, Resource Groups and Resource Explorer. Links to cloud/aws/cost for the reporting side and compares with Azure tags and tag inheritance.

articles.title: Service Quotas and Trusted Advisor: managing limits, throttling and best-practice checks across accounts
articles.scope: Covers applied vs default quotas, account-level vs resource-level quotas, increase requests, quota request templates, Service Quotas Automatic Management, and CloudWatch usage alarms, including pre-raising quotas in DR Regions. Explains Trusted Advisor categories, check availability by support plan (Business Support+, Enterprise, Unified Operations as of 2026), the organizational view, Priority and EventBridge automation.

articles.title: Amazon VPC fundamentals: CIDRs, AZ-scoped subnets, route tables, gateways and the VPC router
articles.scope: Explains VPC and subnet scope (regional VPC, AZ-bound subnets), the five reserved addresses, route tables and the local route, public vs private vs isolated subnets, ENIs, Elastic IPs, DHCP option sets and DNS attributes. Contrasts with Azure VNets, whose subnets span zones, and includes CloudFormation, CDK and Terraform for a three-tier VPC.

articles.title: VPC IP addressing: IPv4 planning, secondary CIDRs, IPv6 and dual-stack, BYOIP, public IPv4 charges and VPC IPAM
articles.scope: Covers CIDR planning to avoid overlap and exhaustion, secondary CIDRs and Network Address Usage metrics, IPv6-only and dual-stack subnets, NAT64/DNS64, and egress-only internet gateways. Explains BYOIP, the cost of public IPv4 addresses, managed prefix lists, and IPAM pools, scopes, tiers and policies across an organization.

articles.title: Security groups vs network ACLs: stateful vs stateless filtering in a VPC
articles.scope: Contrasts stateful, allow-only, ENI-level security groups with stateless, ordered, subnet-level NACLs. Covers ephemeral ports, security group referencing (including across peering, Transit Gateway and Cloud WAN), shared security groups and multi-VPC associations, and common misconfigurations. Rates the mapping to Azure NSGs and ASGs.

articles.title: Internet ingress and egress: internet gateway vs NAT gateway (zonal and regional) vs NAT instance vs egress-only IGW, plus VPC Block Public Access
articles.scope: Compares the egress options on availability, cost and operations, including one NAT gateway per AZ vs a shared one and the 2025 regional NAT gateway that expands across AZs automatically. Covers private NAT gateways, ingress routing and VPC Block Public Access enforced by declarative policy. Maps to Azure NAT Gateway and default outbound access retirement.

articles.title: VPC endpoints: gateway endpoints vs interface endpoints (PrivateLink), private DNS and endpoint policies
articles.scope: Contrasts free, route-table-based gateway endpoints (S3, DynamoDB) with per-AZ, ENI-based, billable interface endpoints. Covers private DNS, endpoint policies, access from on-premises, and centralized endpoints shared through Route 53 Profiles. Maps to Azure service endpoints (close to gateway endpoints) and private endpoints (close to interface endpoints).

articles.title: Publishing private services: PrivateLink endpoint services vs VPC Lattice service networks and resource configurations
articles.scope: Covers the provider side of PrivateLink (NLB- or GWLB-backed endpoint services, acceptance, cross-Region access, a fix for overlapping CIDRs) and VPC Lattice (service networks, HTTP/gRPC/TLS services, auth policies, resource gateways and configurations for TCP resources, service-network endpoints). Shows when each fits SaaS, microservice and multi-account patterns, and maps to Azure Private Link Service (close) and to Lattice, which has no direct Azure equivalent.

articles.title: Connecting VPCs: VPC peering vs Transit Gateway vs Cloud WAN vs PrivateLink vs VPC Lattice vs VPC sharing
articles.scope: Builds a decision matrix on transitivity, CIDR overlap, scale, bandwidth, cost, cross-Region and cross-account support, and operational model. Explains why peering is non-transitive and when a proxy or service-level pattern beats network-level routing. Maps to Azure VNet peering, Virtual WAN and Private Link.

articles.title: AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN: regional hubs vs policy-driven global networks
articles.scope: Covers Transit Gateway attachments (VPC, VPN, Direct Connect gateway, Connect/GRE for SD-WAN, peering, network function, Client VPN), route tables, association vs propagation, blackhole routes, appliance mode, multicast, policy-based routing (2026), 1:1 NAT for overlapping CIDRs (2026), Flexible Cost Allocation and Encryption Support. Contrasts with Cloud WAN's core network policy, segments, core network edges and service insertion. Compares both with Azure Virtual WAN.

articles.title: Multi-account network patterns: VPC sharing, centralized egress, centralized inspection and shared endpoints
articles.scope: Gives reference architectures for a network account owning shared VPCs via RAM, hub-and-spoke with centralized NAT egress, inspection VPCs using Network Firewall or GWLB with appliance mode, centralized interface endpoints with Route 53 Profiles, and east-west vs north-south inspection. Explains trade-offs in cost, blast radius and team autonomy, and maps to Azure hub-spoke and Virtual WAN secured hubs.

articles.title: Hybrid and multicloud connectivity: Site-to-Site VPN vs Direct Connect vs both, SD-WAN, and AWS Interconnect - multicloud
articles.scope: Compares connectivity on bandwidth, latency, encryption, SLA, lead time and cost, including VPN as Direct Connect backup, private IP VPN over Direct Connect, Transit Gateway Connect for SD-WAN, and AWS Interconnect - multicloud (GA with Google Cloud in April 2026, Azure in preview). Maps to ExpressRoute and Azure VPN Gateway.

articles.title: AWS Direct Connect and BGP deep dive: connections, LAGs, VIFs, Direct Connect gateway, MACsec, resiliency models and route control
articles.scope: Covers dedicated vs hosted connections, LOA-CFA, LAGs, private, public and transit VIFs, Direct Connect gateway and SiteLink, MACsec, and the resiliency toolkit models. Explains BGP control: ASNs, communities, local preference, AS_PATH prepending, longest-prefix match and AWS route priority across Direct Connect, VPN and static routes. Includes 2026 features (VIF rate limiters, BGP route visibility, 1,000-prefix limits, flat-rate pricing) and MTU and jumbo frames.

articles.title: AWS VPN and remote access: Site-to-Site VPN, Accelerated VPN, large-bandwidth tunnels, VPN Concentrator, Client VPN and Verified Access
articles.scope: Covers the customer gateway, virtual private gateway vs Transit Gateway termination, two-tunnel design, static vs BGP routing, Accelerated VPN, 5 Gbps large-bandwidth tunnels, VPN Concentrator, CloudHub, and pre-shared keys in Secrets Manager. Compares Client VPN with Verified Access for zero-trust user access, including non-HTTP protocols. Maps to Azure VPN Gateway (S2S/P2S) and Entra Private Access.

articles.title: Amazon Route 53: hosted zones, alias records, routing policies, health checks and DNS resilience
articles.scope: Covers public vs private hosted zones, record types and alias vs CNAME, and every routing policy (simple, weighted, latency, failover, geolocation, geoproximity, IP-based, multivalue) with a comparison table. Also covers health checks (endpoint, calculated, CloudWatch alarm), DNSSEC signing, domain registration, accelerated recovery, and ARC zonal shift. Maps to Azure DNS plus Traffic Manager (partial).

articles.title: Hybrid and multi-account DNS: Route 53 VPC Resolver endpoints, forwarding rules, Profiles, DNS Firewall and Global Resolver
articles.scope: Explains the VPC+2 resolver, inbound and outbound Resolver endpoints, forwarding, system and delegation rules shared via RAM, and private hosted zone association across accounts. Covers Route 53 Profiles, query logging, DNS Firewall including Advanced, DNSSEC validation, and Route 53 Global Resolver (GA March 2026). Maps to Azure DNS Private Resolver and private DNS zones.

articles.title: Elastic Load Balancing: ALB vs NLB vs GWLB, with target groups, cross-zone, stickiness, TLS termination vs passthrough, mTLS and JWT validation
articles.scope: Compares layer 7, layer 4 and layer 3 load balancers by listeners and rules, target types (instance, IP, Lambda, ALB-as-target), health checks, cross-zone behavior, sticky sessions and proxy protocol. Covers TLS policies, mTLS, ALB JWT access-token validation and transforms (2025), NLB QUIC, listener rules and security groups, capacity unit reservation, zonal shift, and the AWS Load Balancer Controller. Maps to Application Gateway, Azure Load Balancer and Gateway Load Balancer.

articles.title: Edge networking: Amazon CloudFront in depth, and how it differs from AWS Global Accelerator
articles.scope: Covers CloudFront distributions, origins and origin groups, cache behaviors and cache, origin-request and response-header policies, OAC, VPC origins, signed URLs and cookies, CloudFront Functions vs Lambda@Edge, Origin Shield, viewer mTLS, multi-tenant distributions and flat-rate plans. Contrasts with Global Accelerator: anycast static IPs, standard vs custom routing, client IP preservation, and non-HTTP and failover use cases. Maps to Azure Front Door and the cross-region load balancer.

articles.title: Network protection services compared: AWS WAF vs Shield vs Network Firewall vs Route 53 DNS Firewall vs Firewall Manager vs security groups
articles.scope: Maps each control to the OSI layer, traffic direction and attachment point it acts on. Covers WAF protection packs (web ACLs), managed rules, Bot Control and rate rules; Shield Standard vs Advanced and the 2026 move to the Anti-DDoS managed rule group; Network Firewall stateless and stateful engines, TLS inspection and the proxy preview; DNS Firewall; and Firewall Manager organization policies. Rates mappings to Azure WAF, DDoS Protection and Azure Firewall.

articles.title: Encryption in transit across AWS networks: Nitro encryption, VPC Encryption Controls, MACsec, IPsec and TLS termination points
articles.scope: Explains which paths AWS encrypts automatically (Nitro instance-to-instance traffic, inter-Region backbone) and VPC Encryption Controls' monitor and enforce modes, Transit Gateway Encryption Support and declarative controls. Covers MACsec on Direct Connect, VPN over Direct Connect, and TLS termination vs passthrough at CloudFront and ELB, using ACM and Private CA. Places each in the shared responsibility model.

articles.title: Troubleshooting AWS networks: VPC Flow Logs, Reachability Analyzer, Network Access Analyzer, Traffic Mirroring, MTU and common failure patterns
articles.scope: A systematic triage path through route tables, security groups, NACLs, NAT, endpoints, DNS and MTU. Covers flow log default and custom fields (including Transit Gateway flow logs), Reachability Analyzer intent checks, Network Access Analyzer scopes, Traffic Mirroring, ELB, WAF and CloudFront logs, and Network Manager Route Analyzer. Links to observability for CloudWatch network monitoring.

articles.title: Network cost on AWS: data transfer, NAT processing, cross-AZ traffic, endpoints, public IPv4 and how to reduce them
articles.scope: Models the main network cost drivers: internet egress, inter-Region and inter-AZ transfer, NAT gateway processing, Transit Gateway data processing (and Flexible Cost Allocation), interface endpoint hours, and public IPv4 charges. Shows ways to cut them: gateway endpoints, CloudFront, AZ affinity, Direct Connect, and the CloudFront and Direct Connect flat-rate plans. Links to cloud/aws/cost for billing tooling.

articles.title: AWS networking cheat sheet: defaults, limits, MTUs, reserved addresses and decision shortcuts
articles.scope: One-page review of VPC, subnet and route quotas, the five reserved IPs, MTU values per path (VPC, peering, Transit Gateway, Direct Connect, VPN, internet), NAT and VPN throughput, the Route 53 routing-policy picker, the load balancer picker, and endpoint type rules. Built for last-week exam review across ANS-C01, SAA-C03 and CloudOps.

articles.title: AWS global infrastructure: Regions, AZs and AZ IDs, partitions, edge locations, Local Zones, Wavelength Zones and Outposts
articles.scope: Explains Regions (and opt-in Regions), AZs and why AZ names differ from AZ IDs between accounts, and the partitions (commercial, GovCloud, China). Covers edge locations and Regional edge caches, and compares Local Zones, Dedicated Local Zones, Wavelength Zones and Outposts racks and servers, with selection criteria for latency, residency and DR. Maps to Azure regions, availability zones, Extended Zones and Azure Local.

articles.title: Amazon EC2 fundamentals: instances, lifecycle, user data, ENIs, status checks and recovery
articles.scope: Covers launching from an AMI with a launch template, key pairs, user data and cloud-init or EC2Launch, and the instance lifecycle (stop, hibernate, terminate, termination protection). Explains ENIs and Elastic IPs, system, instance and EBS status checks, and automatic recovery. Includes C# and Python SDK launch samples plus Bicep-vs-CloudFormation-vs-Terraform equivalents.

articles.title: EC2 instance types and sizing: families, the naming convention, Graviton vs Intel vs AMD, burstable credits and rightsizing
articles.scope: Decodes instance names (family, generation, processor, attributes, size), the general-purpose, compute-, memory-, storage-optimized, accelerated and HPC families, Graviton4 and Graviton5 (M9g, C9g, R9g in 2026), flex instances, and burstable CPU credits with unlimited mode. Covers rightsizing with Compute Optimizer and CloudWatch metrics, and maps families to Azure VM series.

articles.title: EC2 purchasing options: On-Demand vs Savings Plans vs Reserved Instances vs Spot vs Dedicated, Capacity Reservations and Capacity Blocks
articles.scope: Compares commitment, discount, flexibility and capacity assurance. Covers Compute vs EC2 Instance Savings Plans, Standard vs Convertible and regional vs zonal RIs, Spot (interruption notice, rebalance recommendations, allocation strategies), Dedicated Hosts vs Dedicated Instances for licensing, ODCRs including future-dated and interruptible, Capacity Blocks for ML, and RI and Savings Plans sharing across an organization. Maps to Azure reservations, savings plan for compute and Spot VMs.

articles.title: AMIs and image governance: EBS-backed vs instance-store-backed, sharing, encryption, Allowed AMIs, watermarks and EC2 Image Builder
articles.scope: Builds a golden-image pipeline with EC2 Image Builder. Covers AMI copy and encryption across Regions and accounts, sharing and block public access for AMIs, deprecation, ancestry and usage reports, and enforcing Allowed AMIs (including 2026 watermarks) through declarative policies and Config. Maps to Azure Compute Gallery and VM Image Builder.

articles.title: Block storage for EC2: EBS volume types, snapshots, encryption and performance vs instance store
articles.scope: Compares gp3 (up to 64 TiB, 80,000 IOPS and 2,000 MiB/s since 2025), gp2, io2 Block Express, io1, st1 and sc1 with ephemeral NVMe instance store. Covers EBS-optimized throughput, Elastic Volumes, Multi-Attach, encryption by default, snapshots (incremental, Fast Snapshot Restore, archive, Recycle Bin, DLM vs AWS Backup), and diagnosing performance from CloudWatch metrics. Maps to Azure Managed Disks and temporary disks.

articles.title: The Nitro System, enhanced networking and placement groups: performance and isolation under the hood
articles.scope: Explains Nitro cards, the Nitro hypervisor, the Nitro Security Chip, the Nitro Isolation Engine (Graviton5), Nitro Enclaves, NitroTPM, AMD SEV-SNP and bare metal. Covers ENA, ENA Express, EFA and per-instance bandwidth limits, and the cluster, partition, spread and precision-time placement strategies with their limits. Maps to Azure Boost, Accelerated Networking, confidential VMs and proximity placement groups.

articles.title: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling: launch templates, scaling policies, warm pools, lifecycle hooks, instance refresh and mixed instances
articles.scope: Covers Auto Scaling groups across AZs, launch templates vs the deprecated launch configurations, and target tracking, step, simple, scheduled and predictive scaling. Explains health checks and grace periods, default instance warmup, termination policies, warm pools, lifecycle hooks, instance refresh, mixed instances with attribute-based selection, Spot capacity rebalancing, and ELB integration with zonal shift. Maps to VM Scale Sets.

articles.title: Secure EC2 access: IMDSv2 enforcement, instance profiles, EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint, Session Manager and the serial console
articles.scope: Hardens instance access: requiring IMDSv2 and hop limits (account-level enforcement since February 2026), the ImdsV1Enabled metric, instance profiles instead of keys, EC2 Instance Connect and Instance Connect Endpoint vs Systems Manager Session Manager vs bastions, and the serial console. Maps to Azure Bastion, JIT VM access and Azure IMDS.

articles.title: Choosing AWS compute: EC2 vs Lambda vs Fargate/ECS vs EKS vs App Runner vs Elastic Beanstalk vs Lightsail vs Batch
articles.scope: A decision guide covering control, operational burden, scaling granularity, cold start, cost model, statefulness and licensing for each platform. Points to the containers and serverless sections for depth. Pairs each option with its nearest Azure counterpart (VMs, Functions, Container Apps, AKS, App Service, Batch) and a fidelity rating.

terms.definition: The identity created with an AWS account, signed in with the account email address, that has unrestricted access in its own account and is the only identity that can perform a small set of tasks, such as closing the account or changing the support plan.
An identity defined in one AWS account that holds long-term credentials (a console password and/or access keys) and that AWS now recommends only for cases federation and roles cannot cover.
A collection of IAM users in one account that share attached policies; it is not a principal, so it cannot be named in a resource-based policy or assumed.
An identity with permission policies and a trust policy but no long-term credentials, which trusted principals assume through AWS STS to receive temporary credentials.
terms.equivalent: azure: managed identity or service principal plus Azure RBAC role assignment (partial)

terms.definition: A predefined IAM role linked to a specific AWS service, which only that service can assume and whose permissions the service defines; SCPs and RCPs do not restrict it.
terms.equivalent: azure: first-party service principals for Azure resource providers (partial)

terms.definition: A container that passes one IAM role to an EC2 instance, so software on the instance gets automatically rotated temporary credentials from the instance metadata service.
terms.equivalent: azure: system-assigned managed identity on a VM (close)

terms.definition: A JSON permissions policy attached to an IAM user, group or role that states which actions that identity may perform on which resources, under which conditions.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure RBAC role definition plus assignment (partial)

terms.definition: A JSON policy attached to a resource, such as an S3 bucket, KMS key or SQS queue, that names the principals (including other accounts) allowed to act on it, enabling cross-account access without role assumption.
terms.equivalent: azure: resource-scoped role assignment or SAS (partial)

terms.definition: A standalone identity-based policy that AWS creates and updates, such as ReadOnlyAccess, which customers can attach but not edit.
A standalone, versioned identity-based policy that a customer authors in its own account and can attach to many identities.
A policy embedded directly in one user, group or role that is deleted with that identity, used when a strict one-to-one relationship is needed.
The resource-based policy on an IAM role that specifies which principals (accounts, services, federated identity providers) can assume it, and under which conditions.
terms.equivalent: azure: federated identity credential on an app registration or managed identity (partial)

terms.definition: A managed policy set on an IAM user or role as the maximum permissions its identity-based policies can grant; on its own it grants nothing.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure ABAC conditions constraining delegated role assignment (partial)

terms.definition: An inline or managed policy passed when assuming a role or federating a user, which further restricts that single session's permissions to the intersection with the role's policies.
A Deny statement matching a request in any applicable policy; it overrides every Allow, wherever that Allow comes from.
The default denial of any request that no applicable policy explicitly allows, which an Allow added later can overcome.
terms.equivalent: azure: no role assignment grants the action (exact)

terms.definition: The ordered algorithm AWS uses to decide each request: explicit denies win, then RCPs, SCPs, resource-based policies, identity-based policies, permissions boundaries and session policies must each permit it; cross-account requests need an allow in both accounts.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure RBAC evaluation of role and deny assignments (partial)

terms.definition: A named attribute of the request context, such as aws:SourceIp, aws:PrincipalTag or s3:prefix, that a policy Condition element compares using operators like StringEquals or ArnLike.
A global condition key holding the AWS Organizations ID of the calling principal's account, used in resource-based policies to allow access to the whole organization without listing account IDs.

A global condition key containing the ID of the VPC endpoint a request arrived through; the 2025 companion keys aws:VpceAccount, aws:VpceOrgID and aws:VpceOrgPaths match the endpoint owner's account, organization or OU.
terms.equivalent: azure: storage firewall rules for private endpoints and VNets (partial)

terms.definition: A placeholder, such as ${aws:username} or ${aws:PrincipalTag/team}, that IAM replaces with request-context values at evaluation time, so one policy can scope access per principal.
terms.equivalent: azure: ABAC attribute references in conditions (partial)

terms.definition: The globally unique identifier format for AWS resources (arn:partition:service:region:account-id:resource) used in policies, APIs and IaC.
The AWS service that issues temporary, limited-lifetime credentials through APIs such as AssumeRole, AssumeRoleWithSAML, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity and GetSessionToken.
terms.equivalent: azure: Microsoft Entra ID token endpoint (partial)

terms.definition: The STS API that exchanges a JWT from a trusted OIDC identity provider (for example GitHub Actions, Entra ID or Cognito) for temporary role credentials, without any AWS credentials beforehand.
The STS API that exchanges a SAML 2.0 assertion from a corporate identity provider for temporary role credentials, the basis of direct IAM SAML federation.
terms.equivalent: azure: Entra ID SAML SSO to an enterprise app (partial)

terms.definition: Using credentials from one assumed role to assume another role, which limits the resulting session to at most one hour regardless of the role's maximum session duration.
The STS API an authenticated AWS principal calls to obtain temporary credentials for a role it is trusted to assume, which is the standard mechanism for cross-account access.
A secret-like value that a third party must pass when assuming a customer's role, checked by a trust-policy condition to prevent the confused deputy problem.
Key-value attributes passed when assuming a role or federating (often from IdP claims) that act as principal tags for that session and can optionally carry through role chaining.
terms.equivalent: azure: token claims used in ABAC conditions (partial)

terms.definition: An immutable identifier, such as a username, that is set when a role is first assumed, persists through role chaining and is logged in CloudTrail to attribute actions to the original human.

Writing IAM policies that grant access when principal tags match resource or request tags (aws:PrincipalTag, aws:ResourceTag, aws:RequestTag), so permissions scale without a new policy for every team or resource.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure ABAC role assignment conditions (partial)

terms.definition: The AWS workforce identity service that connects an identity source, gives single sign-on to AWS accounts and applications, and grants account access through permission sets assigned to users and groups.
terms.equivalent: azure: Microsoft Entra ID SSO plus Azure RBAC assignments (partial)

terms.definition: An IAM Identity Center template of policies (AWS managed, customer managed, inline, optional permissions boundary) that is provisioned as an IAM role in each account where it is assigned.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure RBAC role assigned to an Entra group at subscription scope (partial)

terms.definition: The user and group store that IAM Identity Center authenticates against: its built-in Identity Center directory, Active Directory, or an external SAML 2.0 identity provider with SCIM provisioning.
terms.equivalent: azure: Entra ID tenant or hybrid identity sync (partial)

terms.definition: An IAM Identity Center capability that carries a user's workforce identity through supporting applications and AWS services, so data access can be authorized and audited per user rather than per application role.

An IAM entity that registers an external SAML 2.0 or OIDC issuer in an account, so its tokens can be exchanged for role credentials; claim checks are mandatory for shared providers such as GitHub Actions.
A feature that lets workloads outside AWS present X.509 certificates from a registered trust anchor (CA) to obtain temporary IAM role credentials instead of long-term access keys.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Arc-enabled server managed identity (partial)

terms.definition: An account-level IAM feature that lets AWS principals call STS GetWebIdentityToken for a short-lived signed JWT, so they can authenticate to external services (including other clouds) without stored secrets.
terms.equivalent: azure: managed identity tokens presented to external relying parties (partial)

terms.definition: A long-term credential pair for an IAM user or root user used to sign programmatic requests; best practice is to replace it with temporary credentials.
An IAM capability that uses automated reasoning to report external, internal and unused access, validate and custom-check policies, and generate least-privilege policies from CloudTrail activity.
terms.equivalent: azure: Entra access reviews plus Defender for Cloud permissions management (partial)

terms.definition: A console and API tool that evaluates which actions a principal's policies (including permissions boundaries and SCP effects) would allow or deny, without making real requests.
terms.equivalent: azure: check access in Azure RBAC (partial)

terms.definition: IAM data showing when principals last used each service and action, plus a downloadable credential report of users' password and key status, used to remove unused permissions and credentials.
terms.equivalent: azure: Entra sign-in logs and access reviews (partial)

terms.definition: A managed user directory and OIDC/OAuth 2.0 authorization server for application end users, with sign-up, sign-in, MFA, social and enterprise federation, and JWT issuance.
A Cognito component that exchanges tokens from user pools, social IdPs or SAML providers (or guest access) for temporary AWS credentials mapped to IAM roles.

The AWS family of directory options: AWS Managed Microsoft AD (a real, AWS-managed AD forest that supports trusts), AD Connector (a proxy to on-premises AD), and Simple AD (a Samba-based, AD-compatible directory).
A managed fine-grained authorization service that evaluates application permissions written in the open-source Cedar policy language, separating authorization logic from application code.

The AWS service that groups accounts into a hierarchy under one management account, providing consolidated billing, organization policies, trusted access and delegated administration for integrated services.
terms.equivalent: azure: tenant root plus management group hierarchy (close)

terms.definition: The account that creates and pays for an organization; it controls policies and membership, is not restricted by SCPs or RCPs, and should therefore run no workloads.
terms.equivalent: azure: billing account owner plus tenant root management group (partial)

terms.definition: Any account in an organization other than the management account; it is subject to inherited organization policies and its usage rolls up to consolidated billing.
A container for accounts and nested OUs (up to five levels below the root) in an AWS organization, used to apply policies to groups of accounts.
The Organizations feature that combines all member accounts' charges into one bill, aggregating usage for volume pricing tiers and sharing Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts.
terms.equivalent: azure: billing account with billing profiles (partial)

terms.definition: An organization authorization policy that sets the maximum permissions available to IAM users and roles (including member-account root) in the targeted accounts; it never grants, and it does not affect the management account or service-linked roles.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy deny effect or deny assignments (partial)

terms.definition: An organization authorization policy (since November 2024) that caps the permissions any principal, including principals outside the organization, can have on resources of supported services in member accounts.

The Organizations policy category enforced in a service's control plane rather than at API authorization, maintaining a baseline configuration even as new APIs appear; it includes EC2, tag, backup, AI opt-out, Security Hub, S3, Bedrock and other policy types.

A declarative policy type that enforces EC2 and VPC account attributes across an organization, such as VPC Block Public Access, Allowed AMIs, image and snapshot block public access, IMDS defaults and serial console access.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy built-ins for VM and network settings (partial)

terms.definition: An Organizations declarative policy that standardizes tag keys, capitalization and allowed values, and can prevent non-compliant tagging operations for specified resource types.
An Organizations declarative policy that controls, across accounts, whether AWS AI services may store and use customer content to improve those services.

A member account registered to administer an integrated service (for example GuardDuty, Config or IAM Identity Center) for the whole organization, keeping day-to-day operations out of the management account.
An Organizations setting that lets a specific AWS service operate across all accounts (creating service-linked roles as needed) to provide organization-wide features.

An IAM and Organizations capability (November 2024) for removing member accounts' root credentials and performing scoped privileged root tasks from the management or delegated account, without root passwords.
terms.equivalent: azure: Entra PIM for Global Administrator (partial)

terms.definition: The AWS service that sets up and governs a multi-account landing zone by orchestrating Organizations, IAM Identity Center, Config and CloudTrail, with managed controls, drift detection and Account Factory.
A pre-configured, governed multi-account AWS environment with baseline identity, logging, security and network accounts and guardrails, usually built with Control Tower or Landing Zone Accelerator.

A Control Tower governance rule that is preventive (SCP, RCP or declarative policy), detective (Config rule) or proactive (CloudFormation hook), with mandatory, strongly recommended or elective guidance.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy assignments in a landing zone (close)

terms.definition: Control Tower's account-vending capability, built on Service Catalog, that creates and enrolls accounts with a standard baseline; Account Factory for Terraform (AFT) offers the same through a GitOps Terraform pipeline.
An open-source AWS solution that deploys a configuration-driven, compliance-oriented multi-account baseline via CDK pipelines, often on top of Control Tower.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Landing Zones Terraform/Bicep modules (close)

terms.definition: A divergence between a Control Tower landing zone's expected configuration and its actual state (such as a moved account or a modified managed SCP); since landing zone 4.0 it is reported through EventBridge.
The AWS service that records resource configurations and their changes over time and evaluates them continuously against rules and conformance packs, with optional automatic remediation.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy compliance plus Resource Graph change analysis (partial)

terms.definition: A point-in-time record that AWS Config creates of a resource's attributes, relationships and metadata whenever the configuration recorder detects a change.
terms.equivalent: azure: Resource Graph resource change record (close)

terms.definition: A desired-state check, either AWS managed or custom (Lambda or Guard), evaluated when configurations change, periodically, or proactively before provisioning, which marks resources compliant or non-compliant.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy definition with audit effect (close)

terms.definition: A deployable collection of Config rules and remediation actions, such as an operational best practices pack for a framework, applied to an account or across an organization.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy initiative / regulatory compliance (close)

terms.definition: An AWS Config resource that collects configuration and compliance data from multiple accounts and Regions, or a whole organization, into one account for central queries.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Resource Graph cross-subscription queries (close)

terms.definition: The AWS service that records API activity and account actions as events, giving an audit history of who did what, from where and when.

CloudTrail's event categories: management events (control-plane), data events (resource data-plane operations such as S3 object access), network activity events (API calls through VPC endpoints) and Insights events (anomalous API rates or errors).
terms.equivalent: azure: Activity Log vs resource logs (partial)

terms.definition: A CloudTrail trail created in the management or delegated administrator account that logs events for every account in the organization, typically to a central Log Archive bucket that member accounts cannot modify.
terms.equivalent: azure: management-group diagnostic settings via Azure Policy (partial)

terms.definition: A CloudTrail feature that writes signed SHA-256 digest files, so you can prove that delivered log files were not modified or deleted after delivery.
A managed store and SQL query engine for CloudTrail and other activity events, closed to new customers from 2026-05-31 while existing customers continue to use it.
terms.equivalent: azure: Log Analytics workspace with Activity Log (partial)

terms.definition: A case-sensitive key-value label attached to an AWS resource, used for organization, automation, cost allocation and tag-based access control.
A resource tag that is activated in the Billing console so that it appears as a dimension in Cost Explorer and cost and usage reports; it can be user-defined or AWS-generated.

terms.term: AWS Resource Groups and Tag Editor
terms.definition: Tools to group resources by tag or CloudFormation stack and to find and bulk-edit tags across Regions; AWS Resource Explorer adds cross-Region and cross-account resource search.
terms.equivalent: azure: resource groups plus Azure Resource Graph search (partial)

terms.definition: The AWS service for viewing default and applied quotas (per account, Region or resource), requesting increases, applying request templates across an organization, and alarming on usage before limits are hit.

An AWS service that inspects accounts and recommends improvements in cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, service limits and operational excellence; full checks require Business Support+, Enterprise or Unified Operations.

The AWS service that shares supported resources, such as subnets, transit gateways, Resolver rules, prefix lists and capacity reservations, with other accounts, OUs or the whole organization without copying them.
terms.equivalent: azure: cross-subscription RBAC plus Azure Lighthouse (partial)

terms.definition: A set of preventive guardrails, built with SCPs, RCPs, resource-based and VPC endpoint policies, that allows only trusted identities to access trusted resources from expected networks.
terms.equivalent: azure: Private Link plus network security perimeter plus tenant restrictions (partial)

terms.definition: An AWS service that lets administrators publish approved CloudFormation- or Terraform-based products with constraints, so users can self-provision compliant resources and accounts.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure managed applications service catalog / template specs (partial)

terms.definition: A logically isolated, Region-scoped virtual network in an AWS account, defined by IPv4 and optional IPv6 CIDR blocks, in which AZ-scoped subnets, route tables and gateways are created.
A range of a VPC's addresses confined to one Availability Zone (with five addresses reserved); it is public if its route table sends traffic to an internet gateway, and private otherwise.
terms.equivalent: azure: VNet subnet, which is regional and zone-spanning (partial)

terms.definition: A set of destination-to-target routes associated with subnets (or with gateways for ingress routing) that the VPC router uses with longest-prefix match; every table includes a non-removable local route.
A horizontally scaled, highly available VPC component that routes traffic between a VPC and the internet and performs one-to-one NAT for instances with public IPv4 addresses.
terms.equivalent: azure: implicit internet routing with public IP (partial)

terms.definition: A stateful VPC gateway that lets IPv6 resources initiate outbound internet connections while blocking unsolicited inbound IPv6 connections.

A managed network address translation service that lets resources in private subnets reach the internet or other networks without accepting inbound connections; zonal gateways live in one AZ, and private NAT gateways translate to private IPs.
A NAT gateway mode (November 2025) that expands and contracts across Availability Zones automatically as workloads move, needs no public subnet, and can draw addresses from IPAM pools.
A self-managed EC2 instance with source/destination check disabled that performs NAT, which is cheaper at low throughput but requires you to handle scaling, patching and failover.
A static public IPv4 address allocated to an account that can be remapped between instances or network interfaces; like every public IPv4 address, it is billed hourly.
A virtual network card in a subnet that carries private and public IPs, security groups and a MAC address, and can be attached to or moved between instances.
A stateful, allow-only virtual firewall attached to network interfaces that filters traffic by protocol, port and source or destination (CIDR, prefix list or another security group).
terms.equivalent: azure: network security group on a NIC plus ASGs (close)

terms.definition: A stateless, subnet-level firewall with numbered allow and deny rules evaluated in order, which needs explicit return-traffic rules for ephemeral ports.
terms.equivalent: azure: NSG on a subnet, which is stateful (partial)

terms.definition: A named, versioned set of CIDR blocks, customer- or AWS-managed (for example CloudFront origin-facing IPs), that can be referenced in security groups and route tables and shared via RAM.

An account- and Region-level setting (November 2024) that blocks traffic through internet gateways and egress-only internet gateways for VPCs and subnets, with exclusions, and can be enforced by declarative policy.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Policy denying public IPs (partial)

terms.definition: A VPC feature (November 2025) that monitors or enforces encryption in transit for traffic within and between VPCs in a Region, using Nitro hardware encryption or application TLS, with a monitor mode and an enforce mode.
A VPC feature for planning, allocating and monitoring IPv4, IPv6 and BYOIP address space across accounts and Regions with scopes, hierarchical pools and allocation rules.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Virtual Network Manager IPAM (close)

terms.definition: A one-to-one, non-transitive private connection between two VPCs (same or different account or Region) with non-overlapping CIDRs; it has no bandwidth bottleneck and no edge-to-edge routing.

A regional, managed hub router that connects VPCs, VPNs, Direct Connect gateways, SD-WAN (Connect) and peered transit gateways through attachments and multiple route tables, enabling transitive routing at scale.

A routing domain inside a transit gateway: each attachment is associated with one table that routes its traffic, and propagates its routes into any number of tables, which allows segmentation such as isolated VPCs with shared services.
terms.equivalent: azure: Virtual WAN hub route tables (close)

terms.definition: A VPC attachment setting that keeps both directions of a flow on the same AZ's network interface, so stateful inspection appliances see symmetric traffic.
A transit gateway attachment type that runs GRE tunnels with BGP to SD-WAN or virtual appliances over a VPC or Direct Connect transport attachment.
terms.equivalent: azure: Virtual WAN NVA in hub / BGP peering (partial)

terms.definition: A managed global WAN service in which a JSON core network policy defines segments, core network edges per Region, attachment rules and service insertion, replacing hand-built transit gateway peering meshes.
A free VPC endpoint for S3 or DynamoDB, implemented as a prefix-list route in route tables, that keeps traffic on the AWS network but cannot be reached from on-premises or peered networks.
A PrivateLink-powered set of ENIs with private IPs in your subnets (billed per AZ-hour and per GB) that gives private, DNS-integrated access to AWS services or endpoint services.

The AWS technology for exposing a service (behind an NLB or GWLB) or resource privately to consumer VPCs through interface or resource endpoints, with one-way connectivity and no need for non-overlapping CIDRs.
A resource-based policy on a gateway or interface endpoint that limits which principals, actions and resources can be reached through that endpoint.

A managed application-networking service that connects, secures (with IAM auth policies) and monitors services and TCP resources across VPCs and accounts through service networks, independent of IP routing.
Sharing subnets of a VPC owned by one account with other accounts in the same organization via RAM, so participants deploy resources into a centrally managed network.

A dedicated or partner-hosted private network connection from on-premises to an AWS Direct Connect location that gives consistent bandwidth and latency; it is not encrypted by default, and MACsec or IPsec is added on top.

A VLAN with a BGP session on a Direct Connect connection: a private VIF reaches VPCs, a public VIF reaches AWS public endpoints, and a transit VIF reaches transit gateways through a Direct Connect gateway.
A globally available construct that links private or transit VIFs to virtual private gateways or transit gateways in any commercial Region; it does not route traffic between the VPCs attached to it.
terms.equivalent: azure: ExpressRoute circuit with Premium / Global Reach (partial)

terms.definition: A bundle of same-speed dedicated connections at one Direct Connect location, managed with LACP as a single logical connection, with a minimum-links setting.
A managed IPsec VPN service in which each connection provides two tunnels between a customer gateway and a virtual private gateway, transit gateway or Cloud WAN, using static or BGP routing.
The AWS-side VPN and Direct Connect concentrator attached to a single VPC, which can propagate learned routes into that VPC's route tables.
The AWS resource that represents the customer's on-premises VPN device: its public IP (or certificate) and BGP ASN.
A transit gateway VPN option that enters the AWS network at the nearest edge location through Global Accelerator, reducing internet path variability.
A managed OpenVPN-based remote-access service that authenticates users with certificates, Active Directory or SAML and places them on VPC networks; native transit gateway attachment arrived in 2026.

A zero-trust access service that evaluates each connection against identity and device-posture policies before granting access to applications, including non-HTTP resources such as SSH, RDP and databases, without a VPN.

A managed private Layer 3 connection with MACsec-encrypted physical links between AWS and other cloud providers (GA with Google Cloud in April 2026; Microsoft Azure in preview), billed hourly by capacity.
AWS's highly available DNS service, combining authoritative public and private hosted zones, domain registration, health checks and traffic routing policies.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure DNS plus Traffic Manager (partial)

terms.definition: A Route 53 container of DNS records for one domain; public zones answer internet queries, and private zones answer only from associated VPCs (including VPCs in other accounts).
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure DNS zone / private DNS zone (close)

terms.definition: A Route 53 extension record that points a name, including the zone apex, at AWS resources such as ELB, CloudFront, S3 websites or VPC endpoints, follows their IP changes automatically, and incurs no query charge for AWS targets.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure DNS alias record set (close)

terms.definition: The rule Route 53 applies to choose answers for a record set: simple, weighted, latency-based, failover, geolocation, geoproximity, IP-based or multivalue answer, optionally combined with health checks.
A Route 53 monitor of an endpoint, other health checks (calculated) or a CloudWatch alarm, whose status drives DNS failover and the removal of unhealthy records.

The recursive DNS resolver available by default in every VPC at the VPC+2 address, which answers for VPC names, private hosted zones and public domains, and extends to hybrid DNS through Resolver endpoints and rules.

ENIs that VPC Resolver creates in your subnets: inbound endpoints accept DNS queries from on-premises or other networks, and outbound endpoints forward queries to external resolvers according to rules.
terms.equivalent: azure: DNS Private Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints (exact)

terms.definition: A VPC Resolver rule that forwards queries for a domain through an outbound endpoint to specified DNS servers; it is associated with VPCs and can be shared across accounts via RAM.
A shareable bundle of DNS configuration (private hosted zones, Resolver rules, DNS Firewall rule groups, interface endpoints) that can be applied to many VPCs and accounts at once.
A VPC Resolver feature that allows, alerts on or blocks outbound DNS queries using domain lists and managed threat lists, with Advanced rules that detect DNS tunneling and DGA domains.
An internet-reachable anycast DNS resolver (GA March 2026) for authorized clients that resolves public and private hosted zones over Do53, DoT and DoH, with filtering, logging and Regional failover.
An AWS service for application recovery that provides zonal shift and zonal autoshift away from an impaired AZ, routing controls with readiness checks, and orchestrated Region switch plans.
AWS's managed load balancing family: Application, Network, Gateway and Classic Load Balancers, which distribute traffic to registered targets across AZs with health checks.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Load Balancer / Application Gateway family (partial)

terms.definition: A layer 7 load balancer for HTTP, HTTPS and gRPC with content-based listener rules, TLS termination, mTLS, OIDC user authentication, JWT access-token validation, and instance, IP or Lambda targets.
A layer 4 load balancer for TCP, UDP, TLS and QUIC with ultra-low latency, a static IP per AZ, client IP preservation and optional TLS termination; it can front PrivateLink endpoint services.
A layer 3 load balancer that transparently distributes traffic over GENEVE (port 6081) to fleets of third-party virtual appliances, reached through Gateway Load Balancer endpoints in route tables.
terms.equivalent: azure: Gateway Load Balancer, which uses VXLAN (close)

terms.definition: A set of instance, IP, Lambda or ALB targets with a protocol, port and health check that listener rules route to; it can be weighted or shared across load balancers.

A load balancer setting that spreads traffic evenly across all registered targets in every enabled AZ rather than per-AZ; it is on by default for ALB, off by default for NLB and GWLB, and inter-AZ charges can apply.
AWS's content delivery network that caches and accelerates HTTP(S), WebSocket and gRPC traffic at edge locations, with cache and origin policies, edge functions, signed URLs and AWS WAF integration.
An AWS point of presence outside the Regions that serves CloudFront, Route 53, Global Accelerator and Shield, backed by larger Regional edge caches for CloudFront.

The CloudFront mechanism that SigV4-signs origin requests so that S3 buckets (including SSE-KMS buckets), Lambda function URLs and MediaPackage origins accept only requests from specific distributions.
terms.equivalent: azure: Front Door Private Link origins / managed identity to storage (partial)

terms.definition: A CloudFront origin type (November 2024) that reaches ALBs, NLBs or EC2 instances in private subnets directly, so the origin needs no public exposure; it can be shared across accounts via RAM.
terms.equivalent: azure: Front Door Premium Private Link origin (close)

terms.definition: CloudFront's two edge-compute options: CloudFront Functions are sub-millisecond JavaScript for viewer request/response manipulation at every edge location, and Lambda@Edge runs Node.js or Python at Regional edge caches with network access, longer runtimes and origin events.

A no-overage monthly plan (November 2025) that bundles CloudFront delivery with AWS WAF, DDoS protection, Route 53 DNS, CloudWatch Logs ingestion, edge compute and S3 credits; blocked attack traffic does not count against usage.

A network-layer service that gives two static anycast IPv4 addresses (or four, dual-stack) entering the AWS backbone at the nearest edge and routing TCP/UDP to healthy Regional endpoints, without caching.

A layer 7 web application firewall whose web ACLs (shown as protection packs in the new console) apply managed and custom rules, rate limits, Bot Control and fraud-control rules to CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito and other resources.
Automatic, no-cost protection for all AWS customers against common layer 3 and 4 DDoS attacks on AWS edge and Regional services.

A paid subscription adding enhanced DDoS detection and mitigation for protected resources, Shield Response Team access, health-based detection, cost protection and layer 7 mitigation through the AWS WAF Anti-DDoS managed rule group.

A managed, stateful network firewall and IPS for VPC traffic, with stateless and Suricata-compatible stateful rule engines, domain filtering, TLS inspection and managed threat rules, deployed via endpoints or transit gateway attachments.
An organization-wide policy service that centrally deploys and audits AWS WAF, Shield Advanced, security group, Network Firewall, DNS Firewall and third-party firewall policies across accounts.

Metadata records of IP traffic to and from network interfaces, subnets, VPCs or transit gateways (addresses, ports, action, bytes and optional extended fields), delivered to CloudWatch Logs, S3 or Firehose; they are not packet captures.
A feature that copies full packets from ENIs, filtered by rules, to an NLB, GWLB endpoint or ENI target for deep packet inspection and troubleshooting.
terms.equivalent: azure: virtual network TAP / Network Watcher packet capture (partial)

terms.definition: A configuration analysis tool that determines, without sending packets, whether a path between two resources is reachable and names the blocking component if not.
terms.equivalent: azure: Network Watcher connection troubleshoot / IP flow verify (partial)

terms.definition: A VPC tool that finds unintended network access paths matching defined scopes, such as internet-reachable databases, to verify segmentation requirements.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Virtual Network Manager verifier (partial)

terms.definition: A VPC feature (March 2025) that peers over BGP with appliances inside a VPC and dynamically updates VPC and gateway route tables for routing fault tolerance.
A separate geographic area containing multiple isolated Availability Zones, which most AWS services are scoped to; newer Regions must be opted in before use.

One or more discrete data centers in a Region with independent power, cooling and networking and low-latency links to the other AZs; account-specific AZ names map to stable AZ IDs (such as use1-az1) that identify the physical zone.

An extension of a Region placed in a metropolitan area that runs a subset of services, such as EC2, EBS and ELB, for single-digit-millisecond latency or local data residency; Dedicated Local Zones are built for a single customer.
AWS compute and storage embedded in telecommunications providers' 5G networks, reached through a carrier gateway for ultra-low-latency mobile edge applications.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Operator Nexus / private MEC (partial)

terms.definition: AWS-owned and AWS-managed racks or servers installed on customer premises that extend a Region's AZ, running EC2, EBS, ECS, EKS, RDS and S3 on Outposts with the same APIs, connected through a service link.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Local (formerly Azure Stack HCI) (partial)

terms.definition: AWS's virtual server service that provides resizable instances of many types, launched from AMIs into VPC subnets and billed per second or hour depending on OS.
A named hardware profile such as m8g.xlarge that encodes family, generation, processor and attributes, and size, and determines vCPU, memory, storage, network bandwidth and accelerators.
An EC2 T-family instance that earns CPU credits below a baseline and spends them to burst; in unlimited mode it can exceed its credits for an extra charge.
AWS-designed Arm64 processors that power the g-suffixed instance families; Graviton5 (M9g, C9g, R9g, GA 2026) includes the Nitro Isolation Engine and usually gives better price-performance than x86.
A Regional template of root volume snapshots, block device mappings and launch permissions used to launch instances; it can be copied, encrypted, shared and deprecated.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Compute Gallery image version (close)

terms.definition: An account-level EC2 setting, enforceable by declarative policy, that limits which AMIs can be discovered and launched by provider, name, age, Marketplace code or (since 2026) provenance watermark.
A managed pipeline service that builds, hardens, tests and distributes AMIs and container images on a schedule or trigger.
A versioned EC2 launch specification (AMI, instance type, network, IAM profile, metadata options, user data) used by RunInstances, Auto Scaling groups and EC2 Fleet.
terms.equivalent: azure: VM Scale Set model / template spec (partial)

terms.definition: The legacy, immutable Auto Scaling launch specification that supports no instance types released after 2022 and cannot be created at all by accounts opened on or after October 1, 2024.
A script or cloud-init directive (up to 16 KB) passed at launch that the instance runs at first boot by default, readable through the instance metadata service.

The link-local endpoint (169.254.169.254) that gives an instance its metadata and role credentials; IMDSv2 requires a PUT-obtained session token and hop limit, mitigating SSRF, and can be enforced per account since 2026.
A VPC endpoint that provides IAM-authorized SSH and RDP to instances in private subnets with no public IP, bastion host or agent required.
Network-attached, AZ-scoped persistent block volumes for EC2 in SSD types (gp3, gp2, io2 Block Express, io1) and HDD types (st1, sc1); gp3 scales to 64 TiB, 80,000 IOPS and 2,000 MiB/s.

An incremental, Regional point-in-time backup of an EBS volume stored durably by AWS, which can be copied across Regions and accounts, archived, protected by Recycle Bin, or pre-warmed with Fast Snapshot Restore.
An io1/io2 feature that attaches one volume to up to 16 Nitro instances in the same AZ, which requires a cluster-aware file system to avoid corruption.
Physically attached NVMe or HDD block storage on the host whose data is lost when the instance stops, hibernates, terminates or its hardware fails, suited to caches, buffers and replicated data.

An EC2 placement strategy: cluster packs instances for low latency in one AZ, partition separates groups across racks, spread places up to seven instances per AZ on distinct hardware, and precision time uses hardware with high-precision time sources.
terms.equivalent: azure: proximity placement group / availability set (partial)

terms.definition: AWS's virtualization platform of dedicated Nitro cards for networking, storage and management, a minimal hypervisor (with the formally verified Nitro Isolation Engine on Graviton5) and a security chip, which isolates customer workloads and allows no operator access to them.

Isolated compute environments carved from an EC2 instance's CPU and memory, with no persistent storage, interactive access or external networking, and cryptographic attestation integrated with KMS for processing highly sensitive data.

The SR-IOV enhanced networking interface on Nitro instances that provides high bandwidth and packets per second; ENA Express uses SRD to raise single-flow throughput and reduce tail latency, and since 2026 also works across AZs.
A network device for HPC and ML instances that adds OS-bypass (libfabric/NCCL) communication over AWS's SRD protocol for tightly coupled MPI and distributed training or inference.
A logical group of EC2 instances spanning AZs that keeps capacity between minimum and maximum, replaces unhealthy instances, and scales according to policies using a launch template.

An Auto Scaling policy that adds or removes capacity to keep a metric, such as average CPU or ALB requests per target, at a target value; it is preferred over step scaling (alarm-threshold bands) and simple scaling (single adjustment with cooldown).
An Auto Scaling policy that forecasts load from historical cyclical patterns and provisions capacity ahead of demand, usually combined with target tracking.
A pool of pre-initialized stopped, hibernated or running instances kept beside an Auto Scaling group, so scale-out skips long boot and bootstrap times.

An Auto Scaling hook that pauses an instance in a Pending:Wait or Terminating:Wait state, so custom actions such as configuration, log drain or deregistration can run before it enters or leaves service.
EC2 capacity paid per second or hour with no commitment, which gives maximum flexibility at the highest unit price and no capacity guarantee.

A one- or three-year commitment to a dollar-per-hour spend in exchange for discounts: Compute Savings Plans apply across EC2 families, Regions, Fargate and Lambda, while EC2 Instance Savings Plans give deeper discounts locked to a family in a Region.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure savings plan for compute (close)

terms.definition: A one- or three-year billing discount for a specific instance configuration; Standard RIs can be resold, Convertible RIs can be exchanged, and only zonal RIs also reserve capacity.
Spare EC2 capacity at steep discounts that AWS can reclaim with a two-minute interruption notice, best for fault-tolerant, flexible workloads diversified across instance types and AZs.
terms.equivalent: azure: Azure Spot VMs, with 30-second eviction notice (close)

terms.definition: A physical EC2 server fully dedicated to one account, with visibility into sockets and cores and control over instance placement, supporting bring-your-own-license for per-socket or per-core software.
An EC2 instance that runs on hardware dedicated to one account but without host-level visibility or placement control, used for tenancy compliance rather than licensing.

A reservation of EC2 capacity for an instance type in a specific AZ, billed at On-Demand rates whether used or not, with no term commitment; it can be future-dated, shared, and (since 2025) made interruptible.
A way to reserve GPU or Trainium instances in co-located clusters for a fixed future window (from one day up to six months), paid upfront, for training and inference bursts.
An AWS service that analyzes utilization metrics to recommend rightsizing for EC2 instances, Auto Scaling groups, EBS volumes, Lambda functions and other resources.
Stopping an EBS-backed instance after saving its RAM to the encrypted root volume, so it resumes with in-memory state and preloaded applications, with no compute charges while stopped.

pairs.difference: Security groups are stateful, allow-only and attached to ENIs; NACLs are stateless, ordered allow/deny rules on subnets, so return traffic on ephemeral ports must be allowed explicitly.
A role has no long-term credentials and issues temporary STS credentials to whoever its trust policy allows; a user holds a permanent password and access keys tied to one identity.
Identity-based policies attach to principals and cannot name a Principal; resource-based policies attach to resources, name principals and can grant cross-account access without role assumption.

Both only cap permissions, but an SCP applies to every principal in the targeted accounts from the organization level, while a boundary applies to one user or role and is set by account administrators.
SCPs cap what your principals can do anywhere; RCPs cap what anyone, including external principals, can do to your resources, and only for supported services.

SCPs filter API authorization and miss new APIs unless written broadly; declarative policies enforce a configuration state in the service's control plane, govern service-linked roles and survive new features.
An explicit Deny overrides every Allow from any policy type; an implicit deny is just the absence of an Allow and disappears as soon as any applicable policy allows the action.

Gateway endpoints are free route-table entries for S3 and DynamoDB that on-premises clients cannot use; interface endpoints are billed per-AZ ENIs with private IPs and DNS, reachable over VPN, Direct Connect and peering.

Peering is a free-of-hourly-charge, non-transitive one-to-one link with no bandwidth bottleneck; Transit Gateway is a billed regional hub with route tables that gives transitive, segmentable any-to-any routing for thousands of attachments.

Transit Gateway is a regional router you mesh by hand with peering and static routes; Cloud WAN is a global network declared in one policy document, with segments propagated automatically across Regions.

PrivateLink exposes one service or resource per endpoint, one-way at layer 4; Lattice joins many services and resources into a service network with layer 7 routing and IAM auth policies, without per-consumer endpoints.
An internet gateway allows two-way internet traffic for resources with public IPs; a NAT gateway lets private resources initiate outbound connections only, hiding them behind its addresses.
A zonal NAT gateway lives in one AZ's public subnet, so high availability needs one per AZ and per-AZ routes; a regional NAT gateway spans AZs automatically and needs no public subnet.

VPN is encrypted IPsec over the internet, available in minutes but with variable latency; Direct Connect is a private physical circuit with consistent performance and weeks of lead time, unencrypted unless MACsec or VPN is layered on.

A private VIF reaches VPCs through a virtual private gateway (or a Direct Connect gateway to VGWs); a transit VIF reaches transit gateways through a Direct Connect gateway, giving one circuit access to many VPCs and Regions.

ALB terminates HTTP(S) and routes on content with layer 7 features such as authentication and JWT validation; NLB forwards TCP, UDP, TLS and QUIC at layer 4 with a static IP per AZ, client IP preservation and much lower latency.
NLB is an endpoint clients connect to; GWLB is a transparent bump-in-the-wire that wraps original packets in GENEVE to inspection appliances and returns them unchanged.

CloudFront caches and terminates HTTP at the edge using DNS names; Global Accelerator does not cache, and gives static anycast IPs that carry any TCP/UDP traffic over the AWS backbone to Regional endpoints with fast failover.

WAF filters layer 7 requests with rules you write or subscribe to; Shield Advanced is a DDoS protection subscription adding SRT support, cost protection and automatic layer 7 mitigation, which itself uses WAF rules.
Config records what a resource looks like over time and whether it is compliant; CloudTrail records which API call changed it, by whom and from where.
An alias works at the zone apex, resolves directly to AWS resource IPs and is free for AWS targets; a CNAME cannot sit at the apex and adds a resolution step.

Savings Plans commit to dollars per hour and apply flexibly across families (and, for Compute Savings Plans, Fargate and Lambda); RIs commit to an instance configuration, and only zonal RIs also reserve capacity.
A regional RI is a billing discount with no capacity guarantee; an ODCR guarantees capacity in one AZ at On-Demand price with no term, and the two can be combined.
Both are single-tenant, but only a Dedicated Host exposes sockets and cores and pins placement, which is what bring-your-own-license software counted per socket or core requires.

EBS volumes are network-attached, persist independently of the instance and can be snapshotted; instance store is physically local NVMe that is faster but lost on stop, hibernate, termination or host failure.

Cluster packs instances close together in one AZ for lowest latency at the price of correlated failure; spread puts each instance on distinct hardware (maximum seven per AZ) to minimize correlated failure.

Launch templates are versioned and support current instance types, mixed instances and new features; launch configurations are immutable legacy objects that new accounts cannot create at all since October 2024.

Identity Center centrally assigns permission sets across every account from one identity source; direct IAM SAML federation needs an identity provider and role mappings configured separately in each account.
A user pool authenticates end users and issues OIDC JWTs for your app; an identity pool exchanges such tokens for temporary AWS credentials to call AWS services directly.
An AWS account carries its own IAM authorization boundary and root user, while an Azure subscription is a billing and RBAC scope inside a tenant whose identities live in Entra ID.

pairs.b: Azure RBAC with Microsoft Entra ID
pairs.difference: IAM writes JSON policies with explicit Deny and rich conditions per account; Azure separates the directory (Entra ID) from role assignments at management-group, subscription, resource-group or resource scope, and customers cannot author general deny rules.

Both give platform-rotated credentials without secrets, but a role is assumed per session and can be shared or chained across accounts, while a managed identity is an Entra service principal bound to resources and authorized through RBAC.
SCPs cap which API actions principals may call regardless of resource properties; Azure Policy evaluates resource properties at create or update and cannot cap a principal's general permissions.

Both are policy-inheritance hierarchies, but OUs nest only five levels deep and carry SCPs, RCPs and declarative policies, while management groups go six levels deep and carry Azure Policy and RBAC assignments.
Control Tower is a managed service with drift detection and Account Factory; Azure Landing Zones is reference architecture plus IaC (Bicep or Terraform) that you deploy and operate yourself.
An AWS subnet is pinned to one AZ, so multi-AZ designs need a subnet per AZ; an Azure subnet is regional and spans zones, with zonal placement chosen per resource.

Both are managed transit hubs with route tables, but Transit Gateway is a pure router to which you attach firewalls, while Virtual WAN hubs bundle VPN, ExpressRoute and Azure Firewall gateways in a Microsoft-managed hub VNet.
An AWS interface endpoint is per service per VPC and fronts the whole regional service; an Azure private endpoint maps to one specific resource instance, such as a single storage account.

A Direct Connect gateway reaches VPCs in any commercial Region from one location; ExpressRoute circuits reach VNets in the same geopolitical region unless Premium is added, and Global Reach links on-premises sites through the Microsoft backbone.

Front Door combines CDN, global layer 7 load balancing across origins and an integrated WAF in one product; on AWS these are CloudFront plus AWS WAF, with Global Accelerator or Route 53 for non-cached global routing.
NLB can terminate TLS, has security groups, gives a static IP per AZ and fronts PrivateLink services; Azure Load Balancer is a pure pass-through layer 4 balancer without TLS termination.
Route 53 combines authoritative DNS, health-checked routing policies and domain registration; Azure splits these across Azure DNS, Traffic Manager and App Service domains.

AWS gives a two-minute interruption notice plus earlier rebalance recommendations and market-based pricing; Azure gives a 30-second eviction notice, with an optional maximum price or capacity-only eviction.
EBS volumes are always AZ-scoped, so cross-AZ resilience relies on snapshots or replication; Azure offers zone-redundant (ZRS) managed disks, which have no AWS equivalent.

pairs.b: Azure RBAC conditions on delegated role assignment
pairs.difference: A boundary caps the effective permissions of any role a delegate creates; Azure conditions only restrict which roles and principals a delegate may assign, not the permissions inside those roles.
